Removing rottay/network-professional@1 from the schema moves the digest back, proving the re-anchor was CAUSED not cosmetic. Registry ids unique, namespaced, versioned, purely additive, no base name reused, schema version unchanged. Receipt: cohort-1-schema-digest-proof.json

centralFinding.title: The reusable semantic-group vocabulary already exists, is fully tenant-writable, and the Cohort 1 families do not consume it.
proof: foundation/themes/default.css defines 8 surface roles x 18 channels = 144 role channels (canvas, shell, panel, card, inset, control, raised, overlay).
Every one is in TENANT_THEME_OVERRIDE_TOKENS, so a DB tenant can author the whole matrix per role.
NOT ONE --ds-button-*, --ds-input-* or segmented token is in that allowlist. Zero.
Button reads only --ds-button-*. The only tenant-reachable dimension of a button was therefore the handful of --ds-button-primary-* values the compiler DERIVES from the palette.
That is the mechanical reason two tenants on one component tree differ on colour and on almost nothing else.

measuredGroupCoherence.definition: shared axes / union of axes across a group's members

mechanismFinding.title: Adoption is not a uniform refactor, and the reason is a CSS fact rather than a preference.
mechanismFinding.law: A role channel declared on `:root` is ALWAYS defined, so var(--ds-material-X, <family>) never reaches its fallback: the role default silently REPLACES the family value. A tenant-writable role channel NOT declared on `:root` behaves the opposite way — the fallback fires, today's paint is preserved exactly, and the channel becomes causal on first tenant write.
mechanismFinding.worked example: --ds-material-control-shadow defaults to `none` while --ds-button-primary-shadow carries a real `0 1px 2px` in several themes. One naive fallback line would flatten every button in every theme while reading, in review, like a no-op refactor.
mechanismFinding.consequence: The safe adoptions land now and are provably paint-preserving. The sighted ones are proposals, and they are stated as proposals rather than merged behind a fallback that cannot fire.

openDefectsFound.title: Elevation is INVERTED between the two tenants.
openDefectsFound.evidence: --ds-elevation-1 is `none` for BitHire and `0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` for The Management; --ds-elevation-2 is `none` vs `0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`.
openDefectsFound.why it is a defect: The Monochrome Executive Ledger is emitting soft blurred ambient shadows, and 'glass, blur, soft floating-card soup' is one of its named forbiddenOutcomes. BitHire, whose direction asks for a low soft shadow on floating regions, is flat. Each tenant has the other's depth posture.
openDefectsFound.constraint: --ds-elevation-1/2/3 are NOT tenant-writable. All 32 --ds-material-{role}-shadow* channels ARE. So the fix is role adoption, and its resting posture is a sighted decision.

openDefectsFound.title: The edge axis is silent for The Management.
openDefectsFound.evidence: BitHire emits --ds-edge-{emphasis,hairline,standard}-width from its expressive profile. The Management emits none, because its document authors no expressive axes at all.
openDefectsFound.why it is a defect: Its direction is built on ruled separation — 'visible black or graphite rules', 'hairline internal dividers, stronger region keylines'. No --ds-edge-* or --ds-divider-* token is in the tenant allowlist, so advanced.profiles is the only route and the document does not use it.
openDefectsFound.candidate: edge:'ruled' emits emphasis 2px / hairline 1px / standard 1px against BitHire's hairline 1px/1px/1px. edge:'inset-double' emits a 3px double rule and is arguably an overreach for a 'precise' dossier. Pending art-direction ruling.

openDefectsFound.title: The published `editorial` expressive TYPE profile contradicts the ledger's own numeric law.
openDefectsFound.why it matters: The Management's direction requires 'precise numbers', 'aligned numbers' and 'tabular accents'. Oldstyle figures are text figures and do not align in a column. So The Management must NOT take the editorial TYPE axis despite being an editorial direction; it keeps its authored typePairing plus explicit families. Recorded so a later cohort does not 'fix' this by selecting the obvious-looking axis.

openDefectsFound.title: TENANT_THEME_OVERRIDE_TOKENS and the document intake schema DISAGREE on the base -background channel of every surface role.
openDefectsFound.evidence: --ds-material-{control,inset,panel,card}-background are all present in TENANT_THEME_OVERRIDE_TOKENS (the 294-entry allowlist), but authoring any of them in a TenantThemeDocument is rejected at intake with 'Field is not part of TenantThemeConfig v1'. The -hover/-active/-selected/-disabled variants of the same channel ARE accepted.
openDefectsFound.howFound: Authoring the role grounds for The Management per the advisor ruling; the compiler refused the document.
openDefectsFound.whyItMatters: This is the reason the segmented track and the quiet button variants still render blue under a monochrome tenant. Re-keying those skins onto --ds-material-control-* was necessary but not sufficient: the role channel's :root default resolves through --ds-surface-control, which is NOT tenant-reachable and therefore leaks from the VERTICAL baseline. The one override that would fix it is allowlisted but unauthorable.
openDefectsFound.correctionToAnEarlierClaim: cohort-1-role-adoptability.json counts these -background channels as tenant-writable because it reads the allowlist alone. That map OVERSTATES tenant reach by one channel per role. The count is wrong in the safe direction for adoption planning but wrong nonetheless, and it is corrected here rather than left standing.
openDefectsFound.proposal: Codex adjudicates whether the schema should accept the base -background channel per role, or whether the allowlist should drop it. They must not disagree.
